transcript.text: My Shark cordless battery got really hot on charge last night and this morning it looks puffed up, the plastic case has split at the seam a bit. Can I still use it till a new one comes? It's the IZ201UK.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A swollen, very hot or chemical-smelling battery can catch fire. Stop using and charging it now, unplug the charger, and if it is safe to move put it somewhere non-flammable away from anything that could burn. Don't puncture, squeeze or try to open the battery, and don't put it in the household bin — take it to a battery recycling point. No, please don't use it, not even briefly while you wait. A lithium-ion battery that has overheated, swollen and split its case has damaged cells inside. It can get hot again, leak or catch fire without warning, whether it's charging, running or just sitting in the vacuum. It shouldn't be used or charged again, and the vacuum and charger shouldn't be used either until someone qualified has looked at them. 1. This is by far the most common cause. Swelling is the typical sign.
2. The charger. A faulty or non-genuine charger can overcharge a pack and make it run hot. This matters because it could do the same to a replacement battery.
3. Heat. 1. Unplug the charger from the wall and leave it unplugged.
2. If the battery comes away easily without forcing it, take it off the vacuum. Never press, squeeze or prise the swollen pack. If it's stuck, leave it in place.
3. Put it outdoors or on a hard, non-flammable surface, away from anything that burns and out of reach of children and pets, until it can be disposed of.
4. Don't put it in the household bin. Take it to your local recycling centre's battery or electricals point and tell them it's swollen. To help pin down the cause, it's worth knowing whether the charger is the original Shark one and how old the battery is. If the charger is non-original, or the battery is fairly new, the charger becomes more suspect and should be checked before it goes near another battery. Shark's customer service will want this information too, and a swollen battery is a fault they take seriously, so contact them, especially if it's still under guarantee. It's also worth checking Shark's website and GOV.UK product safety alerts for any notice covering your model. I'm not aware of one for certain, but it only takes a minute to check.

claimsRejected.claim: The battery pack itself has failed.

candidates: Internal failure of the lithium-ion battery pack (cell fault from age, wear or damage) (high)
Faulty or non-original charger overcharging the pack (medium)
Battery stored or charged somewhere hot, or previously knocked or dropped (low)

reading.symptom: battery overheated on charge and swollen

plan: They asked: "Can I still use it till a new one comes?" - answer that first.

Safety: a battery hazard is active. The fixed safety warning is shown separately, do not repeat it. It must not be used again until a qualified engineer has checked it: say that plainly. You may explain the likely cause and suggest checks that are safe with it switched off and unplugged, but never say or imply that a check could make it safe to use, or that they might not need an engineer.
Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Shark; model IZ201UK.
The fault they reported is: "battery overheated on charge and swollen". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
